question: Is there a family of paths, each ring's linear rule and each contact's law fixed, that is native at every size of its schedule: four rings growing together from 3 to 9 cells (middle-ring contacts antipodal), from 4 to 9 (contacts two apart), or paths growing from 4 to 9 rings?

public_inputs.library: growth_lib.py in this folder (sha256 e0a377996ea598231c07dfb551bfa6594ae72b7a2c3ecb74d02a29c72dda6d19): the schedules and native(), a fail-fast form of path_lib.analyze; path_lib.py of NATIVE-PATH-20261108-001A (sha256 52ce36a513db4fef263abc91d3b852430334e65fac0e146d6d37e8ddd0b060be).
public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 16 worker processes; registered in docs/LONG_RUNNING.md if it runs over ten minutes.
public_inputs.family: Every linear rule (0, 204, 240, 170, 60, 102, 90, 150) on each ring and every law (proposals, or self-blind with each side reading the left, the right or both neighbours) at each contact. Schedules: antipodal (four rings of s cells, s = 3 to 9, c2 and c3 at index s // 2 or s - s // 2 of their middle rings, chosen per ring), two apart (s = 4 to 9, index 2 or s - 2), longer (n = 4 to 9 rings, end rings of 3 cells and middle rings of 5 with every middle ring on one rule and one position, 2 or 3, the inner contacts on one law). Full levels: every family at s = 3, 4 and 5 (the two four-ring schedules coincide at 4 and 5) and at n = 4 and 5: 36,864,000 four-ring and 2,048,000 longer paths. Every family native or undecided at a full level is followed through every size of its schedule.
public_inputs.exactness: Every verdict is exact by the row-sequence reduction (NATIVE-PATH-20261108-001A, Theorem 2); a row sequence that does not repeat within 200,000 lags is undecided and reported as such.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the families or schedules after seeing results
primary_observable: The number of families native at every size of each schedule; the number native at each size among the followed families; the overlaps of the full levels (native at s and s + 1).
cheapest_meaningful_control: growth_lib.native agrees with path_lib.analyze (checked before freezing on 3,000 random paths of the full levels and the 16 known native paths); in the run, the ten smallest native paths of the full levels must agree on their full state spaces.
decision_or_followup_rule: H1, frozen: some family is native at every size of its schedule. If it holds, verify the family, characterise it and seek a proof for every size. If not, record how nativeness falls off with size as evidence that binding at every lag is tied to particular sizes, which puts A34 under challenge.
stop_rule: Stop when every family of the full levels has its verdict and every followed family its verdict at every size.
nonclaims: Exploratory and non-promotable: these families and schedules only.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing: PATH-HYBRID-20261108-001's results had been read (16 native four-ring paths with one rule per ring at 3/5/5/3, none of which survives growth; 1,120 hybrid ones). growth_lib.native was checked against path_lib.analyze on 3,000 random paths (no mismatch) and on the 16 known native paths (all native). run.py --pilot and a timing of 20,000 random paths at each of s = 3, 4 and 5 (25 to 30 microseconds a path) printed no verdict counts; the full levels should take a few minutes on 16 workers, and the following stage depends on how many families are native.
